newsitem.title: INDIA: Northwest to start India flights in June.
newsitem.headline: Northwest to start India flights in June.

text.p: U.S. Northwest Airlines, the world's fourth largest airline, will start flights to India from June 3, connecting Delhi and Bombay with U.S. destinations through Amsterdam, Northwest officials said on Wednesday.

Northwest Airlines Corp will use its partnership with KLM to offer a daily flight service spread between the two airlines and "seamless check-in and connecting services", Northwest said in a statement.
KLM holds a 25 percent stake in Northwest Airlines.
"India will be and is a key part of our expansion plans," David Wookey, Northwest's vice-president, Atlantic region, told a news conference in New Delhi.
Northwest's entry into the Indian market will make it the third U.S. airline to operate in India after Delta Air Lines Inc and United Airlines, a subsidiary of UAL Corp.

"India, with its rapidly expanding economy, is a key business destination. With the international traffic to India expected to grow in excess of 7.0 percent per year over the next five years, we see a tremendous growth in travel from India to Europe and the United States," Wookey said.
Wookey said Northwest was also eyeing an air cargo market in India. "Our cargo people are very interested in the cargo business in India," he said.

He said Northwest expected to set up an office in India by February, and added that the airline already had 250 people working for it in four Indian firms to which it had farmed out computer services.
